extracted.intended_audience: editors of biomedical journals, journal staff who select reviewers, and researchers studying peer review
extracted.subtask_short: peer review quality for medical journals
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating characteristics that predict high-quality peer reviews for manuscripts submitted to a general medical journal, and describing attributes of a 'good review' including time spent and turnaround. Focus is on measurable reviewer traits and review-process metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer training in epidemiology or statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: In logistic regression analysis, the only significant factor associated with higher-quality ratings by both editors and authors was reviewers trained in epidemiology or statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting reviewers, prioritize those with formal training in epidemiology or statistics where possible, as this training was associated with higher-rated reviews in this study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time spent on a review
rubrics_metrics.description: Review quality increased with time spent on a review, up to 3 hours but not beyond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers might aim to spend up to about 3 hours on an average manuscript review; spending longer than 3 hours did not appear to further increase quality according to the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer age
rubrics_metrics.description: Younger age was an independent predictor for editors' quality assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Younger reviewers were rated higher by editors in this dataset; however, this is an observational association and should be interpreted cautiously rather than used as a sole selection criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial board membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews performed by reviewers who were members of an editorial board were rated of poorer quality by authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial-board membership does not necessarily correlate with better-perceived review quality and may in some contexts be associated with lower author ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explained variation by studied reviewer characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: The characteristics of reviewers had little association with the quality of the reviews they produced (explaining only 8% of the variation), regardless of whether editors or authors defined review quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most variation in review quality is not captured by basic reviewer demographics or readily observable traits; selection strategies based solely on such characteristics are unlikely to reliably identify high-quality reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment method: 7-item review quality instrument and multi-rater assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Review quality was assessed independently by 2 editors and by the corresponding author using a newly developed 7-item review quality instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structured, multi-item instruments and multiple raters (editors and authors) to evaluate review quality rather than ad hoc judgments; specifics of the 7 items are not provided in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turnaround time (intended evaluation dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The study aimed to describe characteristics of a good review particularly in terms of time spent reviewing and turnaround time (objective stated), though the abstract reports findings primarily on time spent and not specific turnaround-time results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turnaround time is a relevant dimension when judging review performance; editors should monitor it alongside review thoroughness, but this abstract does not report detailed turnaround-time findings.
